description: User requests active Laya advisories across all Hub entrypoints where typed decisions can materially affect requests, and removal of unnecessary task_id requirements. Wire the shared runtime into repository solve, context-source selection, context shaping and model/retrieval routing where the Hub has current repository-verified evidence and a deterministic baseline. Ordinary request scope has no required or fabricated task/session identity. Keep actual task lifecycle, completion, watchdog, task-scoped memory, and supervised candidates bound to verified Agent OS tasks. Exclude deterministic-only, administrative, mutation, permission and high-impact paths; retain host approval, privacy, and deterministic fallback. Dashboard must separate request/task scope and runtime evidence. Keep provider parity/runtime status and RAG migration tracked separately.

acceptance_criteria: Generated MCP schemas and provider instructions use one active-profile capability/action source and never advertise disabled actions.
High-profile defaults enable intended capabilities; lower profiles omit actions below their minimum tier.
Static and installed skill/prompt surfaces contain no stale fixed action lists that contradict the active schema.
Every enabled public MCP tool/action family has a concrete trigger; active-profile filters suppress unavailable actions.
Semantic review, reasoning, exploration, compression, and delegation are recommended only when the action, backend, permissions, and quality gates pass.
Exact repository search, facts, tests, builds, and deterministic checks retain authoritative Hub/native routes.
Runtime permission, host trust/approval, task scope, and quality checks remain authoritative; Laya cannot grant permissions or execute tools.
A typed host contract records provider/version/surface/session ownership, events, commands, permissions, mode, identity, evidence references, and verification state.
Only Hub-managed sessions with verified identity and permissions qualify for host actions; unknown provider state fails closed.

Laya actively participates in eligible low-risk Hub decisions for every connected provider; valid recommendations affect central routing/context, with deterministic fallback for abstention, failure, invalid scope, or low confidence.
Shadow comparison is optional evaluation, not a blanket prerequisite; raw prompts, transcripts, and source are never stored by default.
Provider observations distinguish proposed, simulated, executed, and verified; permission checks remain unknown unless the host actually verifies them.
Unknown/disconnected provider status is reported uncertain and never represented as a verified handshake.
Codex, Antigravity/Gemini, Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code/Copilot, OpenCode when enabled, and extra configured MCP providers have source-backed surface, install, trust, and verification coverage.
Codex plugins/hooks and all provider-specific packages use currently documented layouts; setup preserves user configuration and never auto-trusts host hooks.
Generated API coverage and agent instructions match actual enabled provider/tool inventory; no provider is described as supported beyond its implemented surface.
Focused checks cover changed decision paths and host adapters; live handshake status is recorded separately for each available provider.

Repository solve and direct repository delegate apply typed model-route advice only when current evidence, at least two digest-verified distinct routes, and an unambiguous deterministic role baseline exist. Map request types to Hub roles; preserve explicit model selection; keep risk/quality gates.
Repository solve can return typed low-risk delegation advice as metadata. It does not alter deterministic worker/critic planning or start delegated work.

Request-scoped context-source decisions need no task_id/session_id. Verify repository evidence and source provenance; taskless memory must be repository-scoped, and taskless outcomes never become supervised candidates.
Only task lifecycle, completion, watchdog, task-scoped memory, and supervised candidate capture require verified Agent OS task/session identity.

Eligible low-risk repository solve requests with verified evidence run taskless subagent-budget advice using deterministic single_agent baseline. Suggestion is metadata only; it never starts or changes worker/agent planning.

Repository-bound delegate, review, reason, and second_opinion apply typed model-route advice without task_id when canonical-root EvidenceStore evidence is current, at least two distinct digest-verified routes exist, and the deterministic role baseline is unambiguous.
review_diff carries authorized root and current verified evidence into bounded review calls, allowing the shared delegate route to apply eligible Laya advice without task identity.

Explicit model selection, missing or stale evidence, ambiguous baseline, high-risk quality floors, deterministic-only operations, mutation/permission paths, and FIM latency contracts retain current authoritative behavior.
Request-scoped typed decisions may influence eligible low-risk route/context choices; telemetry remains request-scoped and never creates task-bound supervised candidates.

Repository-bound generate_tests and non-cascade speculative_draft may apply quality-preserving typed model-route upgrades from current verified source evidence without task_id; explicit draft models and cascade stages stay authoritative.
Long repository-scoped narrative compression may use typed context_budget advice after deterministic compression declines; text remains outside training capture.

Adaptive repository context packs apply typed retrieval_strategy advice without task_id when initial current EvidenceStore evidence supports it; apply a bounded rerun only for valid choices and keep the hybrid baseline on failure.
Direct /api/rag/search reuses only verified typed dense_rag or lexical_bm25 advice, preserves semantic baseline and deterministic fallbacks, and requires no task_id.
Laya dashboard reports uncalibrated model estimates and does not present decision volume, latency, or fallback rate as proof of value.

Request inference is exposed as local_ai_coord(action=laya_decision) through POST /api/laya/decision; it does not require Agent OS task storage but requires a canonical authorized repository and verified evidence.
Candidate review, human labels, snapshots and export remain under curate_dataset; supervised candidate capture requires a verified task/session.
Dashboard reports scope, eligibility, latency, fallback and baseline alignment; baseline agreement is not quality or utility, which require independent matched labeled evaluation.

clarifications.summary: User directs completion of Codex and all other supported providers (including Antigravity and Claude) and rejects Laya remaining shadow-only. References revalidated against current worktree.

User expands Laya to all appropriate Local AI Hub request paths and explicitly removes unnecessary task_id requirements, including subagent-budget advice. Request-only decisions use repository-scoped identity; lifecycle, task-scoped provenance and supervised capture retain verified task/session identity.

User scope requires request-scoped Laya inference callable outside Agent OS task actions; task_id optional for ordinary decisions, while supervised capture remains task-bound. Eligible typed suggestions affect low-risk route/context choices and dashboard distinguishes alignment from quality.

task_endpoint_routing.description:
Finish full supported-provider integration while making Laya active across eligible Local AI Hub request paths. Use verified repository evidence and server-derived deterministic baselines; do not require or fabricate Agent OS task/session identity for ordinary requests. Cover repository solve and direct repository delegate model routing, context/retrieval/next-step decisions, metadata-only delegation and subagent-budget advice, and taskless context-source evaluation. Keep provider-specific surfaces, permissions, privacy and deterministic gates authoritative. Extend eligible request-scope coverage to repository-bound delegate, review, reason, second_opinion and review_diff when current verified evidence and deterministic model-route baselines exist. No task_id/session_id requirement for these requests. Also cover repository-bound generate_tests, eligible non-cascade speculative_draft, and long narrative compression after deterministic fallback, with typed decisions and current verified evidence. Also use verified adaptive context evidence for taskless typed retrieval_strategy advice, with bounded successful rerun and deterministic hybrid fallback. Also cover direct /api/chat and /api/generate model-route advice when the model is omitted and an authorized repository root supplies current evidence; preserve explicit model selection, strip root before forwarding, and keep /api/embed and rootless requests deterministic.
